concept_html:
A dataclass (lesson B2-L2) does not check types. pydantic does. A BaseModel validates and converts data when you build it, and raises one ValidationError that lists every problem. Examples use pydantic 2.12.

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field


class WeightingConfig(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True)

    weight_col: str
    min_base: int = Field(default=50, gt=0)
    cap: float = Field(default=5.0, gt=1.0)


cfg = WeightingConfig.model_validate(yaml.safe_load(text))
  • Field(gt=0, le=10) adds bounds. @field_validator("name") adds your own rule.
  • extra="forbid" rejects unknown keys, so minbase: 30 in a YAML file fails instead of being ignored. The default, "ignore", drops them silently.
  • frozen=True rejects assignment after construction.
  • e.errors() returns a list of dicts with loc, type and msg. Log it as structured data.

pydantic runs in lax mode by default. It converts "30" to 30 and 30.0 to 30, but rejects "thirty" and 30.5. It also converts True to 1 for an int field. Set ConfigDict(strict=True) when inputs must already have the right type.

One gap: model_copy(update={...}) does not validate. cfg.model_copy(update={"min_base": -1}) returns a config with min_base = -1. To change a validated model, build a new one: WeightingConfig.model_validate({**cfg.model_dump(), "min_base": 30}).

Use pydantic for records and settings that arrive from outside: YAML, JSON, API payloads. Use pandera (lesson B5-L1) for whole DataFrames. For a list of records, TypeAdapter(list[Model]).validate_python(rows) validates them in one call.

title: pydantic models for config and input records
why_html:
A weighting config file had cap: 0.5 typed where 5 was meant, and minbase spelt without the underscore. The loader used a plain dict. The cap shrank every weight above 0.5 down to 0.5, which flattened the weighting, and min_base stayed at its default. The report went out with unweighted-looking results.

WeightingConfig.model_validate with gt=1.0 and extra="forbid" rejects both mistakes in one error message, before any data is read.
